title: Exponential, Factorial and Time/Space
welcome_lead: When growth gets explosive — and how memory factors.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: O(2^n), O(n!), time vs space complexity trade-offs.
final_note: Some problems will outrun any computer.

walkthroughs.body_html: An O(2^n) algorithm on n=40 already needs over a trillion steps. Brute-force subset enumeration is O(2^n). Algorithms like travelling-salesman by brute force are O(n!).
Space complexity measures peak memory. Merge sort is O(n) extra space; quicksort is O(log n). Recursive solutions often add stack space proportional to recursion depth.
You can often trade space for time. Memoisation stores subresults so they need not be recomputed — turning O(2^n) Fibonacci into O(n) at the cost of an O(n) table.
